x: Captain William Hawkins came to India in 1608 and reached Mughal Court from Surat in April 1609 AD but did not succeed in getting permission to set up a factory. s: Blue Water Policy is associated with
x:
The Blue Water Policy (Política da Água Azul) was introduced by the Portuguese Viceroy Francisco de Almeida, the first Portuguese Viceroy in India. The main objective of this policy was to establish Portuguese naval supremacy in the Indian Ocean rather than acquiring extensive inland territories. Almeida believed that control over the sea routes would enable Portugal to dominate the lucrative spice trade between Europe and Asia. To implement this policy, the Portuguese developed a strong navy, built coastal forts and attempted to eliminate Arab and other European competitors from maritime trade. Although Almeida emphasized naval supremacy, his successor Afonso de Albuquerque shifted Portuguese policy towards territorial expansion by capturing Goa, Malacca and Hormuz. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).
Exam Note:
• Blue Water Policy – Francisco de Almeida
• Successor – Afonso de Albuquerque
• Aim – Control of Indian Ocean trade

With reference to the Captain Hawkins, which of the following statements is correct?
(1) He came to India in 1611 as an envoy of James-I.
(2) He was very well versed in Turkish language.
x: William Hawkins sailed from the East India Company’s ship and reached to Surat in 1608 A.D. from Hector. After initial resistance from Portuguese, Hawkins arrived at the Mughal Court of Jahangir in Agra in April, 1609 A.D. Hawkins arrived at the Mughal Court with a letter signed by King James I of England, having introduction about Hawkins and the request of Mughal emperor’s favourable treatment for British traders. Therefore, Hawkins mission was a combination fo both, an imperial embassy and a commercial endeavour. He was sent by company, but with the credentials from the King, which made him representative of both– the King and the company, in the eyes of Mughal court. Hawkins was a good speaker of Turkish language. Jahangir was impressed by his knowledge of Turkish language and bestowed Hawkins, with the title of ‘English Khan’. Jahangir also granted Hawkins a mansab of 400. Therefore, statement (I) is false and the statement (II) is true.

The Dutch East India Company (VOC) was established in 1602 to conduct trade in Asia. Initially, the Dutch established trading factories at Masulipatnam, Pulicat, Nagapattinam, and other ports. Among these, Nagapattinam became the chief administrative headquarters of the Dutch settlements in India. From here, the Dutch supervised their commercial activities on the Coromandel Coast, especially the export of textiles, spices, indigo and other commodities. Although Masulipatnam was the first Dutch factory in Andhra, Nagapattinam later became the headquarters. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).
Exam Note:
• Dutch East India Company – Founded in 1602
• Headquarters in India – Nagapattinam
• First Factory in Andhra – Masulipatnam

s: Where was the headquarters of the Dutch East India Company's settlements in India?
x: Pulicat was the Dutch Coromandel headquarters from 1616 to 1690, after which Nagapattinam became the Dutch headquarters in India; Porto Novo was not.

s: In India, among the following locations, the Dutch established their earliest factory at
x: The Dutch East India Company established its first factory at Machilipatnam in 1605, followed by another at Petapuli in 1606. In 1609, the Dutch established a factory at Pulicat, near Chennai, which became the headquarters of their Coromandel Directorate in 1616. They later established trading depots at Nagapattinam, Kochi, Surat, Chinsurah, Agra, and Patna. In 1690, the Dutch shifted their headquarters from Pulicat to Nagapattinam on the southern Coromandel Coast.

s: Which of the following factories of Bengal was established by the Dutch?
x: & (c) The First Dutch Company in Bengal was set up in Pipali (1627 A.D.). About 1676 A.D. Dutches left the factory at Pipali and established new factory at Balasore. The trading in Bengal by Dutches was properly established in 1653 A.D., when they established their establishment in Chinsurah. Around 1656-57 A.D., Dutches properly established their own factory in Chinsurah. Also, Dutches established their factory in Hooghly, as the severe floods in 1600 A.D. in Hooghly trashed the factories established earlier. Hence, it is clear that, Dutches established their own factory at Chinsurah & Hooghly both. From the options, it’s clear that Dutch’s factories were established at Chinsurah (village in Hooghly) along with at Hooghly headquarter. Till the end of 17th century, Dutch companies were established at Qasim Bazar, Patna, Dhaka, Malda, Balasore, etc.

s: Which place is famously known as ‘Dutch Palace’?
x: Mattancherry Palace in Kochi was built by the Portuguese and gifted to the Raja of Cochin in 1555. It was later renovated by the Dutch, and so it is popularly called the Dutch Palace.

s: Why did Dutch East India Company fail to maintain its influence in India ?
o: Portuguese did not allow them to trade in India.
There was a growing interference of Dutch Government in the Company’s internal affairs.
Dutch indulged in forcible religious conversion of the people and thus were expelled by local kings.
The English forces made them to leave India.
x: English rivalry, together with the Dutch defeat at Bedara (1759), made the Dutch withdraw from India. The other options are not supported, since the Portuguese were not what ended Dutch influence.

s: Which one of the following is the correct statement?
o: The modern Kochi was a Dutch colony till India’s Independence.
The Dutch defeated the Portuguese and built Fort Williams in the modern Kochi.
The modern Kochi was first a Dutch colony before the Portuguese took over from them.
The modern Kochi never became a part of the British colony.
x: The Dutch defeated the Portuguese in 1663 and built Fort Williams in Fort Kochi; Kochi later passed to the British, so option 4 is wrong.
